parsed.headline: Advance voter turnout increases for 2026 municipal election in Toronto, Canada

pages.text: Advance voting for Toronto’s 2026 municipal election saw 222,550 eligible voters participate during a six-day period that ended at 7 p.m. on October 11, 2026. According to the City of Toronto, this turnout represents the highest in over a decade and is a nearly 72 per cent increase compared to the 129,000 early votes recorded during the 2023 mayoral byelection. Election day is scheduled for October 26, 2026, at which time voters must visit their assigned voting places as indicated on their Voter Information Card or the Toronto Elections webpage. Voters who requested mail-in ballots were required to return completed packages to Toronto Elections by noon on October 14, 2026, with the city advising the use of 25 secure, indoor, CCTV-monitored yellow drop boxes located in each ward. Additionally, the deadline for third party advertisers to register to spend money promoting or opposing candidates was 4:30 p.m. on October 9, 2026. Registrations for these advertisers must be filed in person at the Toronto Elections City Hall office.

A survey from Liaison Strategies conducted during the advance voting period suggests incumbent Mayor Olivia Chow leads the mayoral race by five points, polling at 51 per cent among decided and leaning voters, while Councillor Brad Bradford polls at 46 per cent. In response to the turnout and polling data, Chow’s team credited the results to the efforts of volunteers campaigning across the city. Conversely, Laryssa Waler, a spokesperson for Bradford’s campaign, stated that the high early turnout indicates voters are making up their minds ahead of the October 26 election day.

Election day is scheduled for October 26, 2026, at which time eligible voters must vote at their assigned locations as indicated on their Voter Information Card or the Toronto Elections webpage. parsed.headline: Demands for transparency regarding GH¢49.7 million South Africa evacuation costs

pages.text: Akosua Manu, an advisor to NPP flagbearer Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, has called for a transparent account of the GH¢49.7 million spent on an evacuation exercise of Ghanaian nationals from South Africa. In a Facebook post on Tuesday, October 13, Ms. Manu demanded answers regarding concerns over payment registers, alleged ghost names, and discrepancies in flight records, stating that the public deserves to know how the funds were used. She suggested that an independent audit should be welcomed if there is nothing to hide and argued that political disagreements regarding service passports should not distract from the financial scrutiny of the expenditure. This demand follows a public disagreement involving the Majority on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration Committee and its Deputy Ranking Member, Nana Asafo-Ayeh, concerning Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa. The Majority has accused Mr. Asafo-Ayeh of character assassination following the Minister's refusal to grant a service passport to Nana Boakye, a former NPP National Youth Organiser and current NPP 2nd Vice Chairman. The Majority claims the Minister acted according to a presidential directive requiring the return of diplomatic and service passports. Salaga South MP Zuwera Ibrahimah Mohammed defended the Minister, stating public officials must operate within the law regarding requests for favors.

The Majority Caucus of the Parliamentary Select Committee on Foreign Affairs has dismissed allegations that funds used to evacuate 1,964 Ghanaian nationals from South Africa remain unaccounted for. During a press conference on October 12, 2026, the Committee Chairman, Dr. Alfred Oko Vanderpuije, stated that the committee received and scrutinized a comprehensive report from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Dr. Vanderpuije noted that on September 18, 2026, the Committee received a report accompanied by an exhaustive roll of all 1,964 evacuees, which included names, dates of birth, passport numbers, professions, contact information, amounts received, and signatures. He stated that not a single name is missing or unaccounted for. The Chairman added that the Ministry provided extensive financial documentation, including receipts for chartered flights, commercial airline tickets, transportation, feeding, accommodation, and other logistics managed by Ghana’s High Commission in South Africa. The documentation also reportedly included evidence of a GH¢16 million donation from Ibrahim Mahama’s Engineers and Planners. These statements were made in response to a press conference held by the Minority Caucus on October 11, 2026, which alleged that substantial sums of public funds used for the evacuation were unaccounted for.

parsed.headline: Unidentified projectile strikes King Khalid international airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

pages.text: An unidentified projectile hit terminal 4 at King Khalid international airport in Riyadh on Sunday, starting a fire that killed one person and injured 11, according to Saudi civil aviation authorities. Air defences also intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of the airport. This strike followed a deadly missile attack on the same facility on October 10, 2026, carried out by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebel group, which killed 13 people and injured more than 300. The Houthis claimed responsibility for several attacks on the airport in the past week, including the October 10 strike. The October 10 attack killed four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a US citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian, and a Sudanese. Following the attacks, Saudi authorities extended the closure of the airport and stated that schools would be moved online until October 8, 2026. In response to the October 10 strike, US President Donald Trump told reporters he was weighing whether to join the Saudi military campaign in Yemen, stating, “We’re going to look into it.” Additionally, the British embassy in Saudi Arabia advised against all but essential travel to Jeddah and Dammam and to avoid almost all airports.

parsed.headline: Prime Minister Carney to attend two Forever Canadian rallies in Alberta

pages.text: Prime Minister Mark Carney has accepted an invitation to attend two Forever Canadian rallies in Alberta ahead of an October 19 referendum. According to CBC Canada, Carney is scheduled to stop in Calgary on October 8, 2026, and in Edmonton on October 9, 2026. The invitation was extended via a social media post on October 12, 2026, by Thomas Lukaszuk, the founder of the Forever Canadian campaign. Lukaszuk stated that Carney's decision to attend is a good sign for the movement and expressed that Albertans would want to hear from the Prime Minister. Lukaszuk, who leads the campaign for the 'remain' side in the upcoming referendum, said he believes Carney has made an effort to address the concerns of Albertans and that the Prime Minister's message regarding federalism should resonate. The announcement follows a Thanksgiving address made by Carney to Albertans from St. Francis Xavier High School in west Edmonton. The upcoming referendum in Alberta will involve voters addressing 10 questions concerning immigration and constitutional issues, including one question on whether the province should remain in Canada or hold a binding referendum on separating.

parsed.headline: Scientists propose regulatory solutions to mitigate risks of the global pet trade

pages.text: Scientists argue that the global pet trade, specifically involving exotic reptiles and amphibians, poses significant risks to biodiversity and potential human health. In a commentary published in the journal Nature, Susan Lieberman, vice president for international policy at the U.S.-based Wildlife Conservation Society, and Sandra Altherr, co-founder and head of science at Pro Wildlife in Germany, suggest that these risks could be reduced quickly if governments implement specific regulatory changes. Lieberman described the international wildlife trade for species such as reptiles and amphibians as a massive experiment regarding the movement of diseases between different parts of the world. Altherr stated that the exotic pet trade could be regulated very quickly to reduce these risks. The experts identified several legal gaps that governments could address, including the lack of legal recourse for countries of origin when species are sold outside their borders. They also argued that the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) often fails to take proactive approaches to protect species before they become threatened, noting that species nearing extinction may not have sufficient time to undergo the CITES listing process. Additionally, the experts noted that international enforcement and penalties for wildlife trafficking remain weak, with Altherr stating that serious offenses often result in little more than fines and that smugglers face high profits with almost zero risk of jail sentences.

parsed.headline: IMF forecasts inflation surge and GDP decline for Bangladesh in FY27

pages.text: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects that inflation in Bangladesh could surge to 10.9 per cent and GDP growth could decline to 3.2 per cent during the 2026-27 fiscal year. These latest predictions, unveiled in the IMF's World Economic Outlook (WEO) during a press briefing in Bangkok, represent a significant increase from the organization's April forecast of 6.0 per cent for inflation. The IMF's projections for the 2026-27 fiscal year are lower than its July prediction of 3.5 per cent GDP growth, which was already below the government's budgetary target of 6.5 per cent for the current fiscal year. Official counts for the first three months of the current fiscal year recorded headline inflation at 8.32 per cent, 8.26 per cent, and 8.34 per cent respectively.

parsed.headline: Police escort Chittagong University Vice-Chancellor and JCD leaders out after 30-hour confinement

pages.text: On the evening of October 13, 2026, police escorted Prof Sheikh Mohammad Shariful Alam, the newly appointed vice-chancellor of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) in Bangladesh, out of his office following a 30-hour confinement. Current and former leaders of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, who had been trapped in the administrative building with the vice-chancellor since noon on October 12, 2026, were also escorted out during the operation. At 6:15 p.m., Chattogram Deputy Commissioner Zahidul Islam Mia and Superintendent of Police in Chattogram Masud Alam entered the building after students opened the gates and brought the vice-chancellor out. The vice-chancellor was subsequently taken away in an ambulance while approximately 150 protesting students chanted slogans and reiterated demands for the reinstatement of former vice-chancellor Prof Abu Sadat Mohammad Sayem. The students, who have been demonstrating for 21 days, had also cut power and water supplies to the building. Demonstrators stated that the vice-chancellor was permitted to leave only on the condition that he would not return to the campus.

During the confinement, the vice-chancellor's health was a central concern. At approximately 11:00 a.m. on October 13, 2026, he reported experiencing chest pain and a headache. At 1:30 p.m., a medical team led by university Medical Centre doctor Shahabuddin examined him, finding his blood pressure to be normal despite discomfort and sweating caused by the lack of electricity and water. Addressing the crowd via megaphone, Deputy Commissioner Zahidul Islam Mia stated that the administration intervened after the vice-chancellor reported feeling unwell due to hypertension and excessive sweating from the heat during his long confinement.

parsed.headline: Widow of man killed in Ontario head-on crash delivers victim impact statement at sentencing hearing

pages.text: During a sentencing hearing in Newmarket, Ontario, Christina Cristillo provided a victim impact statement regarding the death of her husband, Andrew Cristillo, 35, who was killed in a head-on car crash north of Toronto last year. In an audio recording, Cristillo described living with “overwhelming grief, sadness and heartbreak,” stating her husband was the “foundation” of their family and that his death has left a “huge hole” for her and their three young daughters. The crash occurred outside of Whitchurch-Stouffville in August when the vehicle driven by Jaiwin Victor Kirubananthan collided with the Cristillo family car. Andrew Cristillo was pronounced dead at the scene, while Christina Cristillo and their three daughters were hospitalized for injuries; the children received treatment at Toronto's Hospital for Sick Children. Members of the Cristillo family, including Andrew's father and brother, also described the impact of the death during the hearing held on Tuesday. Kirubananthan pleaded guilty in April to dangerous driving causing death, failing to remain at the scene of a crash where death ensued, and three counts of dangerous operation of a vehicle. Police located Kirubananthan in a field the morning after the collision. Kirubananthan was also charged in January 2025 in connection with a separate crash involving Ontario Premier Doug Ford.

parsed.headline: Israel returns 22 ancient artefacts to Greece

pages.text: Israel returned 22 ancient artefacts to Greece on Tuesday, according to Arab News. The items, which include a statue, drinking vessels, and vases, were described by Greek Culture Minister Lina Mendoni as having been “illegally removed” from Greece. The artefacts, which were seized by Israel Antiquities Authority investigators, date primarily to the fifth and sixth centuries BC. The handover took place at a museum in Athens and was conducted by Israel’s ambassador in Athens, Pninat Yanay. Mendoni stated that this is the first time Israel has returned antiquities to Greece and characterized the event as a gesture of “particular significance” that marks the beginning of closer cooperation between the two nations regarding the protection of cultural heritage.
